new_entities.name: API gateway
new_entities.quote: So what exactly is an API gateway? And do you actually need one?

quotes.text: It's a single entry point that sits between your clients and your backend services. Every request goes through the Gateway first. It decides where to send it, whether to allow it, and what to send back.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Compact definition of what an API gateway does.

quotes.text: The Gateway is a single place to revoke access when something goes wrong. If a client's API key is compromised, you revoke it at the Gateway.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete security benefit of centralizing access control.

quotes.text: The real power isn't any single feature. It's the integration. You can add a new security policy without touching the routing. You can change the backend service without changing the client.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why the gateway pipeline matters more than individual features.

quotes.text: So what's your best first move? Centralize authentication at the gateway. Do that before anything else. Pick one service. Move its auth check to the gateway.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear, actionable first step for adopting a gateway.

chapters.title: Part 2: Security at the front door

takeaways: An API gateway gives clients one front door to many backend services and hides where those services live.
Routing, authentication, rate limiting, load balancing and data transformation run in one pipeline with central visibility.
Once you have three or more services or external API consumers, start by centralizing authentication at the gateway, then add rate limiting.
hook: Too many services, each with its own URL, security and error handling? This episode explains the API gateway pattern in plain English for developers and architects building on Azure or any microservices platform, and shows how one front door simplifies routing, security and traffic management.
